Subject: Quick follow-up + next steps from today's call

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

- Scope we covered: Carely wants to surface PHI (patient intake notes + lab result flags) through a clinical-assistant feature. You confirmed initial usage will be US-only and limited to de-identified summarization for the first phase.
- Compliance asks: you requested Redwood's SOC 2 status, whether we can sign a BAA, and which deployment modes are eligible for PHI (hosted + BAA, Dedicated, Private).
- Technical guardrails we discussed: prefix/KV caching disabled for PHI flows unless routed to Dedicated/Private; optional request-level redaction layer in front of the API; audit log retention requirements (7 years mentioned on the call).

Proposed next steps: 
1) I'll send our standard security summary + SOC 2 cert and confirm BAA availability.
2) Can you complete the vendor security questionnaire (you mentioned sending it) — if you share it today we can target returning answers by EOD Friday.
3) We should set a short call with our compliance engineer (Neha) and your security lead to validate deployment boundaries — are you available Friday 11am PT?

Attachments: Cedar (call recording) is in the live notes, and I'll attach our security one-pager in my next message.

Thanks — Avery

Avery — replying with concise, shareable points you can send to Carely now. I also attached our internal copy of the SOC 2 (NDA required) and Redwood_Security_Summary_v2.pdf for the external team.

Answers (short):
1) SOC 2: We have a current SOC 2 Type II (covering security and availability) for the period Jan-Dec 2027. We can share the SOC 2 under a standard NDA within 24 business hours.

2) BAA: Redwood will sign a BAA for PHI processing. Important clarifications: for Hosted deployments we require that PHI traffic be constrained by customer-configured routing and the customer accepts that prefix caching and persistent KV caching are disabled for PHI routes. Audit logs for PHI requests are retained per contract (default: 7 years, can be adjusted). If Carely requires persistent KV cache for PHI functionality, we must move to Dedicated or Private.

3) Eligible deployment modes for PHI (recommended guidance):
- Hosted + BAA: supported if PHI flows are tightly scoped (no persistent caching, request-level logging, region: US only). Good for fast POC and early production with limited surface area.
- Dedicated: recommended when you need predictable throughput, tenancy isolation, and want to enable additional runtime features (longer KV lifetime in a dedicated pool under contractual controls).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): required for regulated workflows that must remain in a customer-managed network or for air-gapped requirements.

4) Redlines/contract asks to flag for legal: add clause for audit access, SOC 2 sharing under NDA, and clear AL/retention settings for PHI. We should also confirm whether Carely's retention rule (7 years) aligns with their regulatory obligations; we can support it.

Next steps: 
- Avery: send Carely the security summary and the SOC 2 NDA link (I copied the Drive link to the related links field).
- I'll join Fri 11am PT to walk the security team through controls. Dev, can you prepare a simple diagram of dataflow for PHI->Hosted vs PHI->Dedicated for the call?

Thanks — Neha
